svg.title: Three capacitors, three jobs — only one of them is about the signal
svg.desc: A comparison of the three capacitor roles in this build: a 1000 microfarad bulk capacitor holding up the whole logic rail, a 100 nanofarad capacitor stiffening one sensor's local supply at the end of a long cable, and a 1 nanofarad capacitor filtering pickup off one signal line at the receiving end. For each: what it is across, where it must physically sit, and what goes wrong without it.
svg.text: Three capacitors, three jobs — and only one of them is about the signal
A capacitor is always the same thing: a low-impedance path for fast changes. What it does is decided entirely by what you put it across.
100 nF
1 nF
already bought on #11c
the one nobody bought
on the #12b order
ACROSS
the whole logic rail
5 V to GND, at the UBEC
ACROSS
one sensor's supply
the latch's own VCC to its own GND
ACROSS
one signal line
OUT to GND, at the Teensy pin
WHERE IT MUST SIT
Anywhere on the rail. It is a
reservoir for the whole box.
WHERE IT MUST SIT
At the bracket, on the sensor.
At the board end it does nothing —
the metre of cable is the problem
it exists to get around.
WHERE IT MUST SIT
At the Teensy, not the sensor.
The pickup happens along the
cable, and the decision is made
at the far end. Filter where you
decide.
WITHOUT IT
A current step somewhere in the
box sags the rail and the Teensy
resets. The whole system drops.
WITHOUT IT
The latch's own supply dips as it
switches, because a metre of wire
cannot deliver fast. It may switch
WITHOUT IT
A motor-edge spike couples onto a
10 kΩ node and the decoder counts
it as an edge. Odometry drifts, and
it looks like wheel slip.
milliseconds — rides out a brownout
microseconds — one switching event
10 µs filter against an 11 ms signal
So: partly
The 1 nF is about the signal — it is the only one of the three that touches a signal line at all. The 100 nF is about the supply, and it
only improves the signal indirectly, by keeping the part that generates the signal properly fed.
The distinction is not academic: it is what decides which END OF THE CABLE each one is soldered to.
And the honest caveat: the circuit works without either of the small two
They are insurance, not function. What they buy is that the failure they prevent is one of the hardest to diagnose on this vehicle —
a count that is slightly wrong, only while the motor is running, and that looks exactly like tyre slip. Fit them from the start;
do not wait to see whether they are needed, because by then you will be debugging a vehicle instead of a bench.
